transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (NovaRetail Head of ML), Marco Diaz (NovaRetail Platform Eng), Sana Patel (NovaRetail CTO)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles. Focus on INT8 vs FP8, expected latency reductions, and potential quality regressions for extraction tasks. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, im alex from redwood, priya my se is on, and we can take this as a product plus bench walkthrough. is this still the right agenda, laura?
[00:12] Laura: yeah this is great, thanks. we want to see how int8 and fp8 would affect our NER and recommendation text gen flows, and then talk about rollout risk.
[00:25] Priya: perfect, quick note i will share a quant profile spreadsheet and a small harness. we usually run a 2 hour bench with customer prompts to get quality vs latency curves.
[00:35] Marco: sounds good. on infra side, we are on GCP, using k8s autopilot, and we have a VPC peering set up for private deployments. also interested in kms integration for key rotation.
[00:50] Alex: got it. we will cover kms and private options briefly, but priya will dig in on perf. quick primer first, for folks who havent seen optimize: it recommends quant profiles and shows expected token latency and relative quality delta.
[01:10] Priya: right. so on int8 we generally see 2x to 3x speedups on the token loop compared to fp16 on our GPUs, fp8 is sometimes a middle ground with different kernel behavior. quality wise int8 can introduce small regressions for low frequency tokens and named entities if not calibrated.
[01:35] Laura: when you say small regressions can you give an example, like how does it affect our NER precision recall?
[01:45] Priya: good question. on sequence labeling tasks we saw recall drop around 1 to 4 percent depending on the model and the prompt distribution. that's with a default int8 profile. with a tuned profile, often you can bring that under 1 percent but it takes the profile tuning and selective keep-in-fp16 for certain layers.
[02:10] Marco: you mentioned selective keep-in-fp16, is that something automated? or we have to hand edit configs?
[02:18] Priya: Optimize can suggest layer selections automatically. the initial run will profile and propose an int8 profile that keeps problematic layers in fp16. you can also override in the console. the profile is stored for the model version so rollouts are repeatable.
[02:35] Sana: how deterministic are those profiles across runs, like if we rerun in a different cluster?
[02:42] Priya: there can be variance depending on kernel selection and microcode. we try to make it stable by pinning kernel families in the profile and recording the hardware sku. full reproducibility is better in Dedicated or Private where the hardware is pinned.
[02:58] Alex: ok, quick demo, priya can you pull up the quant profiles view in optimize.
[03:05] Priya: sure; pulling up the console now. bear with me, its a little slow on my end. all right, so here is the model catalog, we have a test model, and the quant profiles tab shows a baseline fp16 run, int8 draft, and fp8 candidate. you can see expected latency on the left and quality delta on the right.
[03:30] Priya: notice the quality vs latency curve, we plot token latency percentiles and quality delta using your eval set or our default prompts. for nova retail id recommend uploading 2 to 3 prompt sets so the curve reflects your real requests.
[03:50] Laura: is the quality measure ROUGE? or do you support task specific metrics?
[03:56] Priya: we support multiple metrics. for NER you can upload labels and we compute F1. for generative we use BERTscore or ROUGE as configured. the console uses your selected metric for the quality delta.
[04:12] Marco: curious about latency percentiles. we need p99 under 120ms for chat. will int8 safely push down to p99 of 120?
[04:22] Priya: depends on sequence length and batching. on our internal tests with a 32 token average length, int8 reduced p99 by about 40% on A100 style gpus. but if you have long sequences or a cold kv cache, gains are smaller. we recommend running the bench on your prompts to get a realistic p99 estimate.
[04:45] Alex: also call out that autoscaling and batching will interact. sometimes you see latency variance when autoscaling up new instances, and caching strategies for prefix tokens can change observed p99.
[05:00] Laura: ok, two things for us are important. one is that NER precision does not drop more than 2 percent, and two is the cost per million tokens target. how will we estimate cost savings with int8 or fp8?
[05:12] Priya: Optimize shows estimated unit cost changes based on throughput improvements and the model compute footprint. int8 typically reduces cost per token by 30 to 50 percent depending on GPU pricing and batching. fp8 usually lands between fp16 and int8. we will include a cost projection in the spreadsheet.
[05:30] Marco: are there any compatibility issues with our private deployment? we run an on-prem rack sometimes for sensitive traffic.
[05:36] Alex: good point. Private supports the same kernels and quant profiles, but you need to ensure the inference runtime on your hardware has the same optimized kernels. we provide a compatibility checklist.
[05:50] Priya: yes and on KMS, we have integrations with GCP KMS and external HSMs. audit logs are available for inference requests in Private.
[06:00] Laura: you mentioned fallback earlier, how does that work in a live rollout if int8 starts to degrade quality?
[06:06] Priya: we have rollout policies. you can do canary with traffic split and monitor quality metrics. Optimize can run continuous evals on a heldout prompt set and trigger automatic fallback to the fp16 variant if quality drops below your threshold.
[06:25] Laura: is that automated or do we have to wire alerts?
[06:29] Priya: both. you can do automatic fallback or alerting to your incident channel. customers often prefer a manual review on first few rollouts, then enable automatic fallback.
[06:40] Marco: any gotchas with embeddings or reranking?
[06:43] Priya: embeddings are sensitive; int8 quant can introduce vector shifts that affect similarity. for retriever stacks we are conservative and recommend fp16 or tuned int8 with calibration. reranking can be ok but test your metrics.
[06:58] Alex: quick interjection, someone asked in the chat about model names and vendors, we also see competitors like modelco and bigcloudai doing quant offerings, but our differentiation is the end to end recommendation and automated profile suggestions plus the fallback tooling.
[07:18] Sana: what about telemetry and cost allocation? can we get token level cost by route?
[07:24] Alex: yes console gives per-route cost and token breakdown, plus per model and per deployment. you can export to your finops pipeline.
[07:33] Priya: returning to the live demo, here is an example of tuning. we select the int8 candidate and run a quick 15 minute calibration on our infra. you can see certain layers flagged in orange as low confidence, those are candidates to keep in fp16. the UI lets you do a selective keep and recompute the predicted quality quickly.
[08:05] Laura: there are definitely names being mis-typed in the console for our internal models, sometimes it shows reedwood instead of redwood in the transcription fields but thats fine.
[08:15] Priya: yeah transcription mapping is ascii sometimes off.
[08:20] Marco: thanks, the viz looks helpful. for the bench, we will provide 3 prompt sets: NER, short chat replies, and a long form product description generator.
[08:32] Alex: perfect, we will run the bench across int8, fp8, and baseline fp16, sharing p50/p95/p99 and quality deltas.
[08:40] Sana: what about regulatory requirements, retention of logs in the private case, and encryption at rest?
[08:46] Alex: Private supports customer managed keys, full audit logs retained configurable up to 7 years with enterprise plan. we can share the compliance packet after the call.
[08:58] Laura: ok this has been useful. anything else on our side?
[09:05] Marco: one more technical question, does the profile store kernel pins so the same kernel is used on production?
[09:12] Priya: yes we record kernel family and hardware sku in the profile metadata, so if you move from gcp to dedicated we can surface mismatches and suggest re-calibration.
[09:25] Alex: sounds like we have clear next steps. quick recap and owners?
[09:30] Laura: please also include a simple runbook for rollback in the spreadsheet.
[09:35] Alex: will do. recap, Alex sends quant spreadsheet and runbook, Priya runs the bench on our side with the two chosen prompts when we get the prompt sets from laura, laura will provide the sets by 2026-05-04, bench results targeted week of 2026-05-11.
[09:50] Sana: ok thanks everyone.
